{{Short description|Concept in mathematical topology}}
In [[mathematics]], in the field of [[topology]], a [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] [[topological space]] is said to be '''hemicompact''' if it has a sequence of [[compact space|compact]] subsets such that every compact subset of the space lies inside some compact set in the sequence.<ref>{{harvnb|Willard|2004|loc=Problem set in section 17.}}</ref>  This forces the [[union (set theory)|union]] of the sequence to be the whole space, because every point is compact and hence must lie in one of the compact sets.

==Examples==
* Every [[compact space]] is hemicompact.
* The [[real line]] is hemicompact.
* Every [[locally compact]] [[Lindelöf space]] is hemicompact.

==Properties==
Every hemicompact space is [[σ-compact space|σ-compact]]<ref name=":6">Willard 2004, p. 126</ref> and if in addition it is [[first-countable space|first countable]] then it is [[locally compact space|locally compact]]. If a hemicompact space is [[weakly locally compact]], then it is [[exhaustible by compact sets]].

==Applications==
If <math>X</math> is a hemicompact space, then the space <math>C(X, M)</math> of all [[continuous function (topology)|continuous functions]] <math>f : X \to M</math> to a [[metric space]] <math>(M, \delta)</math> with the [[compact-open topology]] is [[metrizable]].<ref>{{harvnb|Conway|1990|loc=Example IV.2.2.}}</ref> To see this, take a sequence <math>K_1,K_2,\dots</math> of compact subsets of <math>X</math> such that every compact subset of <math>X</math> lies inside some compact set in this sequence (the existence of such a sequence follows from the hemicompactness of <math>X</math>). Define [[pseudometric space|pseudometrics]]

:<math>d_n (f,g) = \sup_{x \in K_n} \delta\bigl( f(x), g(x) \bigr), \quad f,g \in C(X,M), n \in \mathbb{N}.</math>

Then

:<math>d(f,g) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^n} \cdot \frac{d_n (f,g)}{1+d_n (f,g)}</math>

defines a [[Metric space#Definition|metric]] on <math>C(X,M)</math> which induces the compact-open topology.
